Senses.Explanation: “Flourishing yellow flowers” travels with the proposition that yellow flowers are wisdom, and the records preserve both affirmation, rejection, and interview testing of that formula. Literally, flourishing or luxuriant yellow flowers : "flourishing yellow flowers." The phrase occurs 57 times in 41 allowlisted texts. Its distinctively Chan deployment is the frequently quoted proposition, "the green bamboo is entirely the body of the teaching; the flourishing yellow flowers are nothing other than wisdom" . The fuller exact yellow-flower formula occurs 18 times in , while "green bamboo" occurs 116 times in 68. The records preserve disagreement rather than a single unopposed gloss. A question to National Teacher Huizhong says that some call the proposition an erroneous saying while others trust it as inconceivable; his recorded answer accepts it by placing bamboo and flowers within the range of the teaching body and wisdom. The same transmitted passage then has a Huayan lecturer ask Dazhu Huihai why he does not permit the formula; Dazhu distinguishes appearing in response to bamboo and flowers from wisdom or the teaching body being located in those objects. Later, Shending Yikui rebukes people who hear the formula, hold rigidly to it, and never shift at all, calling a fitting phrase "a donkey-tethering stake for ten thousand ages" . In another exchange he asks how wisdom is understood when the yellow flowers are right here, and tells the respondent that he has let the yellow flowers down. Chan thus bends a scene of colored plants into a portable, disputed proposition and a live examination question; this entry reports the acceptance, distinction, and correction recorded by the texts without deciding among them.
